Priority Based Selection Hyperparameter 
Analysis Across Three Forecasts
Original moderate stagger and wide stagger datasets
David Long
University of Queensland and Northrop Grumman
14 October 2026
Main finding
The strongest broadly applicable setting for this maintenance-only benchmark is C30, Wide dense ladder. It 
reaches the highest measured worst-day availability on all three datasets. Its largest smoothness penalty relative 
to a separately tuned dataset winner is 0.56 percent. Dataset-specific settings remain preferable when the final 
smoothness improvement matters.
Dataset Initial minimum Default minimum and std Best minimum and std Best setting
Original 15 18 / 1.422087 18 / 1.401929 C57
Moderate stagger 16 19 / 0.911708 19 / 0.883419 C30
Wide stagger 17 20 / 0.616685 20 / 0.586797 C30
The study crosses 58 neighbourhood and selection settings with the actual original, moderate stagger, and wide 
stagger workbooks, producing 174 matched sweep cases. It also records repeat timings, reference checks, and 
any finalist budget extensions. All 203 run records use the same scoring dates and preserve maintenance 
opening states.
The moderate and wide datasets change initial maintenance ages and the required check mix. They are distinct 
problem instances. Their higher input availability is not an optimisation gain on the original forecast. All reported 
gains compare a configuration with the default on the same dataset.
The previous half-step recommendation reaches 19 available aircraft on wide stagger, compared with 20 for the 
default. It therefore loses on the primary objective on that dataset and should not be adopted universally from 
the original-only result.
This report extends the original-only study and replaces its recommendation as evidence for selecting settings across these three forecasts. It 
evaluates maintenance feasibility; operational constraints are audited separately.

The moderate input has three cohorts of eight aircraft with maintenance timelines advanced by one, three, or 
five model years. The wide input has six cohorts of four, advanced by one through six model years. A model year 
is 365 days. Cohort assignment uses the saved generation seed 42 and was not chosen by the optimiser.
The aged fleets can start at A, B, or C within the repeating A B A C A B A D sequence. The existing opening-state 
adapter retains each aircraft's saved sequence index and A, B, C, and D due clocks. Every check that started 
before the benchmark start of 21 January 2026 is frozen. The original dataset retains its production rebuild 
assumption that its opening A cannot precede the first due date.
Changing only FILE_PATH would incorrectly reconstruct the aged fleets as if all aircraft were at the original 
opening A position. The study instead reads .scratch/initial-maintenance-stagger/schedule-data.json and replays 
the correct opening state. Check counts, types, durations, and these opening clocks remain fixed within each 
dataset.
Unchanged A B C D rules respectively use durations of 14 28 84 126 days, intervals of 365 730 1460 2920 days, and early allowances of 42 
70 70 70 days. These are domain inputs, not search hyperparameters.
All datasets have 24 aircraft, but their D counts and downtime differ. Mean availability should therefore not be compared across datasets as 
a pure measure of optimiser quality.

Priority based selection across three forecasts | 3
Matched dates objective and validation
All three inputs are scored from 2026-01-21 through 2038-01-18, inclusive, for 4381 daily observations. The 
internal coordinate origin is 2025-11-16, allowing checks that began before the scoring dates to retain their full 
intervals. The model horizon is day 4546 and includes the full ends of supplied checks crossing the forecast 
boundary.
The objective is the lexicographic tuple (minimum availability, negative population standard deviation, mean 
availability). A higher worst day outranks every smoothness gain. Scores are calculated with the same NumPy 
functions used by the production method, on the matched visible window. The algorithm never accepts a worse 
endpoint.
The earlier report used 4481 observations through 28 April 2038. The matched study uses the published 4381-
day forecast through 18 January 2038. Checks crossing either boundary remain in the model. Their starts can 
change the maintenance counted inside the visible window, so the visible mean can change even though full 
check durations are conserved. Standard deviations from the two horizons must not be compared directly.
Verification of the study driver
All settings preserve legal starts, no overlap, the maintenance sequence, and due resets. Each endpoint is 
checked by complete rule replay. Daily availability is independently recomputed by the delta-array method and 
by aircraft occupancy masks. Incremental availability must match both exactly. Past checks, opening states, 
check counts, and durations are preserved, and every accepted score strictly improves.
Priority groups are cached within an iteration, unchanged maintenance intervals are omitted from availability 
updates, and clearly dominated proposals are screened conservatively. Retained proposals still receive the 
original exact score. Cached and reference neighbour lists match for every initial configuration and every final 
neighbourhood. Reference original-input runs also match complete trajectories and final schedule hashes after 
these performance changes.
The live source was reorganised under vn_priority_based_selection.py during execution. The sweep processes 
had already loaded the preceding version. Serial repetitions therefore load byte-identical frozen algorithm and 
adapter snapshots whose hashes match all sweep records. This prevents a source-version change from being 
mixed into the timing or quality comparison.
The 58-case sweeps run as independent processes. Their elapsed times are retained as audit observations but are excluded from 
performance comparisons. Finalist timing runs execute serially after all sweeps finish.

rank equally on all inputs because the maintenance overlaps and feasible windows differ. A wide step can pass

counting prefixes as independent runs.

Half steps adds intermediate offsets inside each level. Dense pairs adds separate intermediate levels. These 
differ because the search restarts at its first level after every accepted move and takes the first neighbourhood 
containing an improvement. A union of offsets, a layered ladder, and a reversed ladder can follow different 
trajectories even when they use similar magnitudes.
The ablations restore one half-step level to its original pair while retaining the other levels. Local refinements 
add two-day finishing, forty-two-day initial movement, or twenty-one-day offsets within the first level. Their 
effects are conditional on the remaining ladder and should not be added together as independent contributions.
Complete ordered shift tuples for every setting are provided in the final catalogue. Some structures occur with more than one selection 
policy.

First level finds the first priority level containing any improving candidate and selects the best candidate in it. All 
levels selects the best improving candidate over every priority level in the active neighbourhood. First improving 
stops at the first improving candidate in deterministic order. Priority ties follow start date, aircraft name, check 
index, and offset order.
All policies use the same acceptance rule, so all-level selection does not permit a lower worst day. Differences in 
final smoothness arise from different accepted paths. This crossed comparison tests whether a policy 
recommendation made on the original data also holds on the aged fleets.
Within this interaction matrix, original is strongest with C02, first level, reaching 18 available aircraft and 
standard deviation 1.404088.
Within this interaction matrix, moderate stagger is strongest with C49, first improving, reaching 19 available 
aircraft and standard deviation 0.885310.
Within this interaction matrix, wide stagger is strongest with C49, first improving, reaching 20 available aircraft

This table filters the measured endpoints by the saved operational requirements and includes the unchanged 
input when it passes. It answers which tested snapshot is strongest among those that pass every scenario check. 
It is not a run of an optimiser that enforces those checks during search.
Input means that the unchanged forecast outranks every passing optimisation endpoint in the tested set. None 
means no tested endpoint or unchanged input passes the scenario. It does not establish mathematical 
infeasibility of the scenario or show that a constrained search cannot find a better schedule.
Post-search filtering can discard a strong trajectory after it has already taken an unacceptable move. Enforcing 
displacement limits, busy periods, and dependency groups during proposal generation would produce different 
accepted paths and potentially different best settings. The primary recommendations in this report apply to the 
maintenance-only benchmark until that separate constrained study is performed.

Before the first forecast D check, smaller checks do not reset its opening D clock. With a 126-day duration and 
70-day early allowance, every legal placement covers the 56-day interval beginning at that D due date. The peak 
overlap of these forced intervals bounds the worst day at 18 for the original and 21 for each stagger input. A 
measured result matching its bound proves optimality of the primary objective under those assumptions; 
otherwise the remaining gap is unresolved.
These bounds do not establish globally optimal smoothness. The study is a broad discrete sweep on three 
related forecasts, including two synthetic maintenance-age variants, and uses each saved maintenance opening 
state. It does not establish performance on an independent real fleet, changed maintenance rules, other horizon 
lengths, or operationally constrained neighbourhoods.
The study retains each supplied check list rather than generating additional check cycles when rebuilds change 
dates near the forecast boundary. This matches the fixed-list baseline. A planning implementation that 
regenerates the forecast and adds newly required checks would need a separate verification of the resulting 
schedules and parameter ranking.
Run .scratch/priority-hyperparameter-analysis/run_three_datasets.py with --dataset original, moderate, or wide 
and --sweep-only for the independent sweep processes. After every sweep finishes, run 
finalise_three_datasets.py to obtain serial finalist timings and cap extensions, including the shared setting. The 
script resumes only against matching input, opening-state, frozen algorithm, frozen adapter, and configuration 
records.
The per-dataset JSON files store scores, traces, audits, proposal counts, source hashes, and endpoint schedule 
hashes. Complete schedule JSON files are retained under three-dataset-schedules. The input workbooks, saved 
opening state, production optimiser, and operational configuration are not edited by the study.
The earlier original-only Word report remains an archive for its longer scoring horizon and small legal start perturbations. Those 
perturbations are separate from the actual moderate and wide maintenance-age datasets analysed here.
